Sample.evidence_source: [/page/6/Text/10] A 2 (Condition; Intervention vs Control) × 2 (Time; Baseline vs Post-Intervention) mixed factorial ANOVA was conducted to investigate the effect of the intervention on BDI scores. As can be seen in Fig. 2, the analysis revealed no significant main effect of condition or time [F(1, 18) = 0.54, p = .474, η^2 = .03 and F(1, 18) = 0.96, p = .341, η^2 = .05 respectively], and did not reveal a significant interaction between condition and time [F(1, 18) = 0.02, p = .893, η^2 < .01].
Sample.warning: N derived from ANOVA degrees of freedom (df_error + df_condition + 1 = 18 + 1 + 1 = 20). This is the N for the analysis, not necessarily the total randomized sample.

IPT.evidence_source: [/page/6/Text/6] For the between-group comparisons, the intervention and wait-list control participants completed all pre-post measures. Therefore there was no missing data. A series of t-tests were conducted to check for baseline differences between the treatment group and the wait-list control group (see Table 1).
IPT.warning: Intervention type not explicitly named as CBT, but no mention of IPT or interpersonal therapy. Assumed CBT-like.

dxgive.evidence_source: [/page/6/Text/11] A second 2 (Condition) × 2 (Time) mixed factorial ANOVA was conducted to investigate the effect the programme had on depression levels, however this time with the DASS depression subscale.
